# dlasdt

> Creates a tree of subproblems for bidiagonal divide and conquer.

<section class="usage">

## Usage

```js
import dlasdt from '@rreusser/blahpack/lapack/dlasdt';
```

### Layout API

Takes a storage layout (`order`) and leading dimensions, like CBLAS/LAPACKE.

```js
dlasdt(
    N,
    lvl,
    nd,
    INODE, strideINODE,
    NDIML, strideNDIML,
    NDIMR, strideNDIMR,
    msub
) → Int32Array
```

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `N` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Number of diagonal elements of the bidiagonal matrix |
| `lvl` | `Int32Array` | **out** · Single-element array; on exit, the number of levels on the computation tree |
| `nd` | `Int32Array` | **out** · Single-element array; on exit, the number of nodes on the tree |
| `INODE` | `Int32Array`<br><sub>length N</sub> | **out** · Output array for centers of subproblems (0-based) |
| ↳ `strideINODE` | `integer` | Stride length for `INODE` |
| `NDIML` | `Int32Array`<br><sub>length N</sub> | **out** · Output array for row dimensions of left children |
| ↳ `strideNDIML` | `integer` | Stride length for `NDIML` |
| `NDIMR` | `Int32Array`<br><sub>length N</sub> | **out** · Output array for row dimensions of right children |
| ↳ `strideNDIMR` | `integer` | Stride length for `NDIMR` |
| `msub` | `integer` | Maximum row dimension each subproblem at the bottom of the tree can be of |

<details>
<summary>Reference notes for each argument (the reference implementation's own documentation; 1-based indices)</summary>

- `N`: On entry, the number of diagonal elements of the bidiagonal matrix.
- `lvl`: On exit, the number of levels on the computation tree.
- `nd`: On exit, the number of nodes on the tree.
- `INODE`: On exit, centers of subproblems.
- `NDIML`: On exit, row dimensions of left children.
- `NDIMR`: On exit, row dimensions of right children.
- `msub`: On entry, the maximum row dimension each subproblem at the bottom of the tree can be of.

</details>

**Returns** `Int32Array`

### Strided (strided) API

Takes explicit strides and offsets for every array. Use it for views, sub-matrices and non-unit strides.

```js
dlasdt.strided(
    N,
    lvl,
    nd,
    INODE, strideINODE, offsetINODE,
    NDIML, strideNDIML, offsetNDIML,
    NDIMR, strideNDIMR, offsetNDIMR,
    msub
) → Int32Array
```

Create a tree of subproblems for bidiagonal divide and conquer.

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `N` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Number of columns |
| `lvl` | `Int32Array` | **out** · Single-element array; on exit, the number of levels on the computation tree |
| `nd` | `Int32Array` | **out** · Single-element array; on exit, the number of nodes on the tree |
| `INODE` | `Int32Array`<br><sub>length N</sub> | **out** · Input array |
| ↳ `strideINODE` | `integer` | Stride length for `INODE` |
| ↳ `offsetINODE` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Starting index for `INODE` |
| `NDIML` | `Int32Array`<br><sub>length N</sub> | **out** · Input array |
| ↳ `strideNDIML` | `integer` | Stride length for `NDIML` |
| ↳ `offsetNDIML` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Starting index for `NDIML` |
| `NDIMR` | `Int32Array`<br><sub>length N</sub> | **out** · Output array |
| ↳ `strideNDIMR` | `integer` | Stride length for `NDIMR` |
| ↳ `offsetNDIMR` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Starting index for `NDIMR` |
| `msub` | `integer` | On entry, the maximum row dimension each subproblem at the bottom of the tree can be of. |

<details>
<summary>Reference notes for each argument (the reference implementation's own documentation; 1-based indices)</summary>

- `N`: On entry, the number of diagonal elements of the bidiagonal matrix.
- `lvl`: On exit, the number of levels on the computation tree.
- `nd`: On exit, the number of nodes on the tree.
- `INODE`: On exit, centers of subproblems.
- `NDIML`: On exit, row dimensions of left children.
- `NDIMR`: On exit, row dimensions of right children.
- `msub`: On entry, the maximum row dimension each subproblem at the bottom of the tree can be of.

</details>

**Returns** `Int32Array`: `NDIMR`

</section>

<section class="notes">

## Notes

-   `dlasdt()` corresponds to the reference LAPACK routine [`DLASDT`](https://github.com/Reference-LAPACK/lapack/blob/v3.12.0/SRC/dlasdt.f).

</section>

<!-- /.notes -->

<section class="examples">

## Examples

```js
import Int32Array from '@stdlib/array/int32/lib/index.js';
import dlasdt from '@rreusser/blahpack/lapack/dlasdt';

// Build the divide-and-conquer computation tree for a bidiagonal matrix of order 20 (leaf size <= 5):
const N = 20;
const MSUB = 5;
const lvl = new Int32Array( 1 );
const nd = new Int32Array( 1 );
const INODE = new Int32Array( N );
const NDIML = new Int32Array( N );
const NDIMR = new Int32Array( N );

// Using the standard interface:
dlasdt( N, lvl, nd, INODE, 1, NDIML, 1, NDIMR, 1, MSUB );
console.log( lvl[ 0 ], nd[ 0 ], INODE.subarray( 0, nd[ 0 ] ), NDIML.subarray( 0, nd[ 0 ] ), NDIMR.subarray( 0, nd[ 0 ] ) ); // eslint-disable-line no-console

// Using the strided interface:
dlasdt.strided( N, lvl, nd, INODE, 1, 0, NDIML, 1, 0, NDIMR, 1, 0, MSUB );
console.log( lvl[ 0 ], nd[ 0 ], INODE.subarray( 0, nd[ 0 ] ), NDIML.subarray( 0, nd[ 0 ] ), NDIMR.subarray( 0, nd[ 0 ] ) ); // eslint-disable-line no-console
```

</section>
